action.rationale: Fresh start (evals_used=0) on a 6D deterministic, cheap problem with budget=100; per principle 1 we should learn the landscape first. Probing (~12% ≈ 12 evals) will inform whether to go global (CMA-ES/TuRBO/GP-BO) or local (LBFGSB/BOBYQA) without wasting budget.

Probes suggest a multi-basin landscape (P2 fdc_spearman=0.1905, top10_spread_vs_uniform=1.091) in 6D with cheap, deterministic evaluations, so a global population method is appropriate. It's ambiguous whether CMA-ES or TuRBO will dominate, so we’ll hedge with a small race, warm-started from the archive (current best y=0.3230). This preserves most of the 92 evals left for the winner to exploit.

CMA-ES won the race (0.3149 vs TuRBO 0.3258) and has not yet continued post-race (evals_in_tenure=0), with sigma=0.284 and popsize=9 suitable for further progress in 6D. With 68 evals left and only 9 stall evals since the last improvement, continuing CMA-ES for a full round is the most data-supported next step.

CMA-ES is still making progress (0.0176 over its 30-eval tenure) and is neither converged nor exhausted (sigma=0.239, generation=4), though we've stalled for 10 evals. With 38 evals left, one more CMA-ES round is a good trade to seek further gains before a brief final polish.

Only 8 evaluations remain and CMA-ES has stalled for 40 evals at 0.297346; with popsize 9 it likely cannot complete another full generation. A local polish (L-BFGS-B) from the incumbent is the best chance to squeeze a final improvement on this deterministic, cheap 6D problem.

Only 1 eval remains (evals_left=1) and the active L-BFGS-B is exhausted (exhausted=true) after 7 evals with no improvement, while stall_evals=47. Switching to GP-BO leverages the 99 archived evaluations to make a single model-guided infill on this deterministic problem, giving the best chance for a last-step gain.
